name: Executive Order of July 13, 1880 (Fort Berthold Reservation boundaries)
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty; the nations did not sign it. It changed the reservation the three nations had kept from the 1851 Fort Laramie treaty, which recognised their territory south and west of the Missouri River between the Heart and Yellowstone rivers.
The order added a tract north-east of the Missouri to the reservation in exchange for Fort Laramie treaty lands south of the river (as the ICC described it in Docket 350-A).

breaches.what: By executive order the President took from the Fort Berthold Reservation lands south of the Missouri that the nations held under the 1851 Fort Laramie treaty, giving land north-east of the river in exchange. The Indian Claims Commission records the exchange; the nations' claim for the difference in value went to trial.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Executive Order of July 13, 1880, as described by the Indian Claims Commission in Docket 350-A (1968) and Docket 350-D (1976)

source.title: Three Affiliated Tribes v. United States, Docket 350-A, Opinion of the Commission (1968), 20 Ind. Cl. Comm. 37
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.what: The nations' claim for the difference in value between the lands lost and the lands added by the 1870 and 1880 executive orders was tried on value and then settled by a $3,200,000 compromise judgment, without a finding.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Docket 350-D, 37 Ind. Cl. Comm. 519 (1976)

source.title: Three Affiliated Tribes v. United States, Docket 350-D, Final Award (1976), 37 Ind. Cl. Comm. 519
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.what: The MHA Nation says the 1851 Fort Laramie treaty recognised over 12 million acres as its homeland and that later treaties, executive orders and Acts of Congress reduced this to less than 3 million.
breaches.whoFoundIt: MHA Nation (Three Affiliated Tribes), History page

compensation: No payment at the time. Docket 350-D was compromised for $3,200,000 in 1976.
today: The north-east tract added in 1880 was ceded in turn under the 1886 agreement ratified in 1891 (see cession-1891-03-03-gros-ventre-mandan).

nationVoice.summary: Counts the executive orders and federal acts after 1851 as the steps by which over 12 million recognised acres became less than 3 million.
